note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a TUV 6; A06b TUV 6; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 7 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: No provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad (the dataset codes no separate descent rule for a child born in the country, birth there giving it; the parent's sex is read from mode A01b). Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Tuvalu, 2024
sources.said: Residence in Tuvalu for 7 years. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... No provision ... Generally applicable provision ... A person born outside Tuvalu on or after the date the Constitution took effect (1 October 2023) is a citizen of Tuvalu by birth if on the date of his birth either of his parents is, or would but for their death have been, a citizen of Tuvalu. ... Generally applicable provision ... A person born in Tuvalu on or after the date the Constitution took effect (1 October 2023) is a citizen of Tuvalu by birth. Exceptions: If neither parent is a citizen and person's father (or mother if born outside marriage) was a diplomat in Tuvalu, or neither parent is a citizen and person's father (or mother if born outside marriage) was a citizen of a country at war and birth occurred in occupied territory. ... No provision
